input.requirements: unique takes an array of numbers or strings and returns a new array containing only the first occurrence of each distinct value, in original order. Number 1 and string "1" remain distinct. Do not mutate the input. Empty arrays return empty. Non-array inputs throw TypeError.

context.content: export function unique(xs){if(!Array.isArray(xs))throw new TypeError();return [...new Set(xs)];}

tasks.instructions: Create test/unique.test.js as a runnable ES module using node:test and node:assert/strict, importing unique from '../src/unique.js'. Derive literal expected arrays from the independent requirements, without Set or implementation-derived oracles. Cover empty and singleton arrays, already-distinct values, repeated numbers and strings, and interleaved duplicates whose first-occurrence order differs from sorted order. Verify mixed number 1 and string "1" remain distinct and strings preserve case. Assert each result is a new array, including empty and already-distinct inputs, and that input contents remain unchanged after calls. Include a frozen input containing duplicates to check that mutation is unnecessary. Assert TypeError for representative non-array inputs: undefined, null, booleans, numbers, strings, plain objects, and array-like objects. Keep cases deterministic and avoid unspecified behavior for unsupported array element types. Expected results and error assertions must cite the supplied requirements as their independent basis.
